canonicalPlan.intro: I’d keep this deliberately loose: one coastal-and-Crescent City day, one northern redwoods day around Jedediah Smith, and one Prairie Creek day anchored by the Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway. That gives you different landscapes without turning the trip into a checklist, and leaves room to linger when a grove or beach feels worth it. I couldn’t verify distances or difficulty for the two named Coastal Trail sections, so treat those as optional, self-paced walks rather than promised easy mileage; the visitor centers are good places to choose a same-day walk that suits you. Highway 101 currently has multiple construction-related traffic stops between Orick and Crescent City, so leave the order of the first and third days flexible and avoid stacking fixed-time plans around the drive.

narrativeSections.heading: Keep the pace easy
narrativeSections.markdown: Start each park-focused day with the nearby visitor center, then make just one walk or outdoor anchor the priority. Visitor-center hours and individual trail access can vary, so confirm them on the day—especially if you are relying on a particular walk.

stops.name: Crescent City Information Center
stops.note: Begin with park orientation and ask which nearby redwood and coastal options are most comfortable for an unhurried day.
stops.why: A simple start before choosing how much walking feels right.

stops.name: Coastal Trail: Crescent Beach
stops.note: Make this your one outdoor anchor and walk only the portion that feels enjoyable; no distance or difficulty details were verified here, so keep the turnaround flexible.
stops.why: A named coastal outing near Crescent City that gives the day a scenic focus without needing a packed schedule.

stops.name: Crescent City Information Center picnic area
stops.note: Use the picnic area for a relaxed break rather than adding another destination.
stops.timeWindow: Midday or whenever you return from the coast

stops.name: Hiouchi Visitor Center
stops.note: Start with exhibits on Tolowa culture, redwood ecology, and park information; it is 9 miles east of Crescent City on Highway 199. Ask for a short, current walking recommendation in the Jedediah Smith area.
stops.why: It gives you local context and a practical way to select a walk that matches your relaxed pace.

stops.name: Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park campground area
stops.note: Spend the main part of the day in this northern redwoods setting, using the campground-area visitor center for information before deciding on any walk. Specific trail distances and difficulty were not verified, so do not commit to a route until you check locally.
stops.why: This is the best place in this plan to slow down and make the big-tree experience the point rather than adding more driving.

stops.name: Jedediah Smith Visitor Center
stops.note: Stop for park information and exhibits near the campground amphitheater. Its operations are seasonal, so confirm it is open before relying on it.
stops.why: A low-key finish that helps with next-day planning.

days.label: Prairie Creek and the Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway

stops.name: Prairie Creek Visitor Center
stops.note: Begin with the exhibits on CCC history and redwood ecology, then ask about a short, suitable walk or pullout for the day.
stops.why: It places you in the heart of Prairie Creek and lets you tailor the outdoor portion to that day’s conditions.

stops.name: Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway
stops.note: Let the parkway be today’s primary scenic experience, with time to stop only where access and conditions allow. No verified drive duration or specific pullouts were provided, so keep this unhurried and flexible.
stops.why: A scenic-drive anchor fits your preference for seeing the redwoods without rushing between long hikes.

stops.name: Coastal Trail: DeMartin
stops.note: If you still want a second outdoor stop, take a self-paced look at this named Coastal Trail section. Its distance and difficulty were not verified, so it is optional rather than a required hike.
stops.why: It adds a distinct coastal finish only if you still have energy after the parkway.
